# frozen_string_literal: true

# Factory (Fabrication) profiler. NOT loaded by default; opt in with:
#
#   bundle exec rspec spec/models --require ./docs/test-performance/tools/fabricate_stats.rb
#
# Writes tmp/perf/fabricate_stats.txt with, per factory name:
#   * create/build call counts (top-level + nested)
#   * EXCLUSIVE time (time spent in that factory, minus nested Fabricate calls)
#   * INCLUSIVE time (including nested Fabricate calls)
#   * SQL statements and INSERTs issued while that factory was the innermost frame
#   * RSA(2048) keygen count issued while that factory was the innermost frame
# Plus: share of total example time spent inside Fabricate, and the top spec files
# by number of top-level factory calls.
#
# Overhead: a few clock reads + one AS::Notifications subscriber per SQL. Use the numbers
# for relative shares; absolute times are inflated slightly.

require 'openssl'

module FabStats
  STATS = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = { create: 0, build: 0, excl: 0.0, incl: 0.0, sql: 0, inserts: Hash.new(0), rsa: 0 } }
  STACK = [] # frames: { name:, start:, child: 0.0 }
  FILES = Hash.new(0) # spec file -> top-level Fabricate calls
  TOTALS = { top_incl: 0.0, sql: 0, rsa: 0, rsa_time: 0.0, example_time: 0.0 }

  def self.now = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)

  def self.wrap(kind, name)
    frame = { name: name, start: now, child: 0.0 }
    STACK.push(frame)
    STATS[name][kind] += 1
    if STACK.size == 1
      ex = RSpec.current_example
      FILES[ex ? ex.metadata[:file_path] : '(no example)'] += 1
    end
    begin
      yield
    ensure
      STACK.pop
      elapsed = now - frame[:start]
      STATS[name][:excl] += elapsed - frame[:child]
      STATS[name][:incl] += elapsed
      STACK.last[:child] += elapsed if STACK.any?
      TOTALS[:top_incl] += elapsed if STACK.empty?
    end
  end

  module Wrapper
    def create(name, overrides = {}, &)
      FabStats.wrap(:create, name) { super }
    end

    def build(name, overrides = {}, &)
      FabStats.wrap(:build, name) { super }
    end
  end

  module RSAProf
    def new(*args, **kw, &)
      return super unless args == [2048] && kw.empty?

      if FabStats::STACK.any?
        FabStats::STATS[FabStats::STACK.last[:name]][:rsa] += 1
      end
      FabStats::TOTALS[:rsa] += 1
      super
    end
  end
end

# Test-only speed-up for password hashing.
#
# `User#password=` (Devise) hashes the password with BCrypt on every assignment, and
# BCrypt's cost is floored at 4 (~1.2 ms per call) even though `Devise.stretches` is 1
# in test. Every `Fabricate.build(:account)` builds a local user, so a typical spec
# hashes the same '123456789' thousands of times.
#
# Digests are memoized per (model class, password) for the test process only. Every
# digest is still a real BCrypt hash, so `Devise::Encryptor.compare` keeps working; the
# only difference is that identical passwords share a salt.
module DeviseDigestCache
  CACHE = {}

  def digest(klass, password)
    CACHE[[klass.name, klass.stretches, klass.pepper, password]] ||= super
  end
end

Devise::Encryptor.singleton_class.prepend(DeviseDigestCache)
EOF

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Factory (Fabrication) profiler. NOT loaded by default; opt in with:
#
#   bundle exec rspec spec/models --require ./docs/test-performance/tools/fabricate_stats.rb
#
# Writes tmp/perf/fabricate_stats.txt with, per factory name:
#   * create/build call counts (top-level + nested)
#   * EXCLUSIVE time (time spent in that factory, minus nested Fabricate calls)
#   * INCLUSIVE time (including nested Fabricate calls)
#   * SQL statements and INSERTs issued while that factory was the innermost frame
#   * RSA(2048) keygen count issued while that factory was the innermost frame
# Plus (deterministic, machine-load independent):
#   * total SQL statements, total Fabricate create/build calls, real BCrypt hashes,
#     total Ruby object allocations inside examples
# and the spec files with the most top-level factory calls.
#
# Overhead: a few clock reads + one AS::Notifications subscriber per SQL. Use the numbers
# for relative shares; absolute times are inflated slightly. Prefer the deterministic
# counters when comparing variants on a noisy host (see docs/test-performance/README.md).

require 'openssl'

module FabStats
  STATS = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = { create: 0, build: 0, excl: 0.0, incl: 0.0, sql: 0, inserts: Hash.new(0), rsa: 0 } }
  STACK = [] # frames: { name:, start:, child: 0.0 }
  FILES = Hash.new(0) # spec file -> top-level Fabricate calls
  TOTALS = { top_incl: 0.0, sql: 0, rsa: 0, bcrypt: 0, fab_calls: 0, alloc: 0, example_time: 0.0 }

  def self.now = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)

  def self.wrap(kind, name)
    frame = { name: name, start: now, child: 0.0 }
    STACK.push(frame)
    STATS[name][kind] += 1
    TOTALS[:fab_calls] += 1
    if STACK.size == 1
      ex = RSpec.current_example
      FILES[ex ? ex.metadata[:file_path] : '(no example)'] += 1
    end
    begin
      yield
    ensure
      STACK.pop
      elapsed = now - frame[:start]
      STATS[name][:excl] += elapsed - frame[:child]
      STATS[name][:incl] += elapsed
      STACK.last[:child] += elapsed if STACK.any?
      TOTALS[:top_incl] += elapsed if STACK.empty?
    end
  end

  module Wrapper
    def create(name, overrides = {}, &)
      FabStats.wrap(:create, name) { super }
    end

    def build(name, overrides = {}, &)
      FabStats.wrap(:build, name) { super }
    end
  end

  module RSAProf
    def new(*args, **kw, &)
      if args == [2048] && kw.empty?
        FabStats::STATS[FabStats::STACK.last[:name]][:rsa] += 1 if FabStats::STACK.any?
        FabStats::TOTALS[:rsa] += 1
      end
      super
    end
  end

  module BCryptCount
    def create(*, **, &)
      FabStats::TOTALS[:bcrypt] += 1
      super
    end
  end
end

RSpec.configure do |c|
  c.around do |example|
    t = FabStats.now
    a = GC.stat(:total_allocated_objects)
    example.run
  ensure
    FabStats::TOTALS[:example_time] += FabStats.now - t
    FabStats::TOTALS[:alloc] += GC.stat(:total_allocated_objects) - a
  end

  # Patch at suite start: Fabrication/Rails are not loaded yet when `--require` runs.
  c.before(:suite) do
    Fabricate.singleton_class.prepend(FabStats::Wrapper)
    OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.singleton_class.prepend(FabStats::RSAProf)
    BCrypt::Password.singleton_class.prepend(FabStats::BCryptCount)

    ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe('sql.active_record') do |*args|
      ev = ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event.new(*args)
      next if ev.payload[:cached] || ev.payload[:name] == 'SCHEMA'

      FabStats::TOTALS[:sql] += 1
      next if FabStats::STACK.empty?

      stat = FabStats::STATS[FabStats::STACK.last[:name]]
      stat[:sql] += 1
      stat[:inserts][Regexp.last_match(1)] += 1 if ev.payload[:sql].to_s =~ /\AINSERT INTO "?(\w+)"?/i
    end
  end

  c.after(:suite) do
    s = FabStats::STATS
    tot = FabStats::TOTALS
    total_ex = tot[:example_time]
    lines = []
    lines << format('examples wall time (sum of example.run): %.1fs', total_ex)
    lines << format('time inside top-level Fabricate calls:    %.1fs (%.1f%%)', tot[:top_incl], tot[:top_incl] * 100 / [total_ex, 1e-9].max)
    lines << "DETERMINISTIC total_sql=#{tot[:sql]} sql_under_factories=#{s.values.sum { _1[:sql] }} fabricate_calls=#{tot[:fab_calls]} bcrypt_hashes=#{tot[:bcrypt]} allocations=#{tot[:alloc]} rsa_2048=#{tot[:rsa]}"
    lines << ''
    lines << '== by factory (sorted by EXCLUSIVE time)'
    lines << format('%-34s %7s %7s %9s %9s %7s %7s %6s  %s', 'factory', 'create', 'build', 'excl(s)', 'incl(s)', 'sql', 'insert', 'rsa', 'top INSERT tables')
    s.sort_by { -_2[:excl] }.first(60).each do |name, h|
      ins = h[:inserts].sort_by { -_2 }.first(4).map { |t, n| "#{t}=#{n}" }.join(' ')
      lines << format('%-34s %7d %7d %9.2f %9.2f %7d %7d %6d  %s', name, h[:create], h[:build], h[:excl], h[:incl], h[:sql], h[:inserts].values.sum, h[:rsa], ins)
    end
    lines << ''
    lines << '== INSERTs by table (under factories, all factories)'
    by_table = Hash.new(0)
    s.each_value { |h| h[:inserts].each { |t, n| by_table[t] += n } }
    by_table.sort_by { -_2 }.first(25).each { |t, n| lines << format('%7d %s', n, t) }
    lines << ''
    lines << '== top-level factory calls by spec file (top 40)'
    FabStats::FILES.sort_by { -_2 }.first(40).each { |f, n| lines << format('%7d %s', n, f) }

    FileUtils.mkdir_p('tmp/perf')
    File.write('tmp/perf/fabricate_stats.txt', lines.join("\n") + "\n")
    puts lines.first(4)
  end
end
EOF
